name: Timing belt kit — belt, tensioner and idler
summary: K4M timing service. Renault’s procedure requires replacing the belt, tensioner and idler together; exact timing tools and locking sequence are essential.
safety: Support the engine securely before removing the right-side engine support or timing covers.
Do not rotate the engine backwards. Incorrect timing can cause severe engine damage.
Do not crank or start the engine with timing components removed.
tools: Timing locking pins and camshaft alignment tools

removal.text: Disconnect the battery, remove the right-front wheel and liner as needed, and support the engine before loosening its mount.
Remove the auxiliary belt and covers required to expose the timing drive; install the crankshaft and camshaft locking tools at the prescribed references.
Confirm the crankshaft is seated against its TDC pin and the camshaft grooves align with the locking tool before removing the old belt.
Replace the belt, tensioner and idler. Inspect sealing surfaces and keep oil or grease off the belt and timing drive.
Fit the belt in the specified order, set the tensioner indicator and tighten the idler, tensioner and crank pulley fasteners to their sourced stages.

installation.text: Remove the locking tools only at the prescribed point, then rotate the crankshaft by hand in its normal direction for two complete revolutions.
Return to TDC without impact, recheck the timing marks and tensioner index, and repeat the setup if either is out of position.
Refit covers, mount, wheel and auxiliary belt; reconnect the battery only after all tools and fasteners are accounted for.

checks: Timing locks fit without force at TDC.
Tensioner index remains aligned after hand-rotation and recheck.
No belt contamination, abnormal noise or warning lamp after reassembly.

faults.symptom: No-start or uneven running after belt work
faults.causes: Incorrect crank/cam timing, misplaced belt, or tension outside the specified indicator position.
Incorrect tension, pulley misalignment, or a worn roller.

name: Water pump
summary: K4M pump access requires removal of both the accessory and timing belts; renew the pump sealing and restore coolant and timing correctly.
safety: Work only with the engine cool enough to open the cooling circuit safely.
Support the engine before removing any engine support or timing covers.
Do not scrape or gouge the aluminum sealing face.

parts.name: Water-pump sealant / seal
parts.notes: K4M procedure specifies a thin Loctite 518 sealing bead rather than a conventional gasket.

removal.text: Drain coolant through the lower radiator hose after the engine has cooled and protect electrical accessories from coolant.
Remove the accessory belt, then lock and remove the timing belt using the K4M timing procedure.
Remove the timing tensioner as needed for pump access, then remove the pump. Clean the aluminum mating face without scratching it.

installation.text: Apply the specified Loctite 518 bead and limited thread-sealant drops only at the points described by the K4M procedure.
Install the pump and tighten the M6 and M8 fasteners in the prescribed order to their separate sourced torques.
Restore the tensioner and timing belt, refill and bleed the cooling circuit, and reconnect the battery after reassembly.

checks: No coolant seepage at the pump joint.
Timing marks and belt tension remain correct after hand-rotation.
Coolant level and cabin heater operation are stable after bleeding.

faults.causes: Damaged or contaminated mating face, incorrect sealant bead, or uneven tightening.
Incorrect belt routing, tensioner position, or timing alignment.

name: Accessory (auxiliary) belt
summary: K4M accessory-belt service. The fetched Renault procedure specifies an automatic tensioner for air-conditioned K4M applications and requires renewal of a removed belt.
safety: Disconnect the battery before working near the alternator and rotating belt drive.
Never run the engine without the accessory belt; the source warns of crankshaft accessory-pulley damage.
Do not rotate the engine backwards.

sources.title: Renault Mégane II workshop manual: Courroie d’accessoires
sources.locator: « Remplacer impérativement une courroie d’accessoires déposée »

torques.notes: No K4M-with-air-conditioning tightening value was stated on the fetched procedure page.

removal.text: Disconnect the battery. Raise and support the right-front corner, then remove the wheel, wheel-arch liner and access braces as required.
Release the automatic tensioner in the direction specified for the K4M application and remove the belt.
Inspect pulley alignment and the tensioner for binding, noise or damaged surfaces.

installation.text: Route a new belt over every pulley using the correct vehicle layout and maintain control of the tensioner while fitting it.
Release the tensioner gradually and check that every rib is seated. Refit the liner and wheel, then reconnect the battery.
Turn the engine by hand as appropriate and inspect belt tracking before starting.

checks: Belt ribs are seated on all pulleys.
Tensioner moves smoothly and belt tracks centrally.
No belt squeal or charging warning after start.

name: Thermostat / water outlet
summary: Thermostat replacement procedure and K4M-specific fastener data were not verified in the fetched sources; values are intentionally withheld.
safety: Allow the engine and cooling system to cool fully before opening the system.
Never open the expansion tank or bleed screw while the engine is hot or running.

torques.notes: No K4M thermostat-housing torque was verified.

removal.text: Drain coolant safely and protect electrical connectors from spills.
Label and disconnect the hoses and electrical connector at the thermostat housing, then remove the housing without damaging its mating face.
Check the old seal and housing for corrosion, cracks or deposits.

installation.text: Install the correct thermostat with a new seal and reconnect the hoses and connector without twisting them.
Refill and bleed using the K4M cooling-system procedure; inspect for leaks as the engine warms.

checks: Cooling fan operation and cabin heat are normal.
No leaks at the housing or hose joints.
Coolant level is stable after cooling.

name: Radiator
summary: Radiator removal requires front-end access and draining coolant. The source cautions against damaging radiator, condenser or intercooler fins.
safety: Work with a cool engine and collect coolant for proper disposal.
Avoid bending air-conditioning pipes or damaging heat-exchanger fins.
Disconnect the battery before removing front-end electrical connectors.

torques.notes: No K4M radiator fastener torque was verified.

removal.text: Disconnect the battery, remove front access panels and detach the front fascia and carrier as needed for the specific body configuration.
Drain coolant through the lower radiator hose, then disconnect radiator hoses and fan electrical connectors.
Release the radiator without straining air-conditioning lines; separate the fan assembly if needed.

installation.text: Install the radiator and fan, reconnect hoses and electrical plugs, and secure the front carrier without crushing fins.
Refill and bleed the cooling system, reconnect the battery, and check for leaks and fan operation.

checks: No leaks at hose joints or radiator seams.
Fan operates and airflow through the heat exchangers is unobstructed.
Cooling system is bled and coolant level remains stable.

name: Coolant drain, refill and bleed
summary: Renault’s fetched cooling procedure describes draining, refill through the expansion tank, bleeding, then an automatic degassing cycle.
safety: Drain only with the engine warm-but-safe as specified; never rinse a hot engine.
Never open the expansion tank or bleed screws with the engine hot or running.
Keep coolant away from electrical parts and collect it for safe disposal.

specs.label: Coolant flush temperature
specs.value: Drain with the engine warm; rinse and refill with the engine warm or cold

removal.text: Protect electrical accessories and open the lower radiator hose and the identified bleed points to drain the circuit.
For flushing, close the bleed points, refill with clean water, drain again and restore the lower hose and clips.
Open the water-outlet and heater-hose bleed points, fill through the expansion tank, and close each bleed point when coolant flows continuously.

installation.text: With the engine stopped and air conditioning disabled, complete the fill and refit the expansion-tank cap.
Run the automatic degassing procedure without opening the hot system; top up only after observing the specified safe procedure.
Check for leaks, heater output and coolant freeze protection using an approved tester.

checks: No air pockets or leaks.
Cabin heater works and radiator fan cycles normally.
Recheck coolant level only after the engine has cooled.

name: Sump / oil pan
summary: K4M lower-sump removal requires underbody access and careful cleaning and sealing. The fetched Renault procedure specifies the pan fastener torque and staged tightening sequence.
safety: Support the vehicle securely on rated stands or a lift.
Drain engine oil before removing the sump.
Use care around the aluminum sealing faces; excess sealant can contaminate the engine or cooling system.

removal.text: Drain the engine oil, remove the undertray and the required wheel-arch and lower crossmember supports.
Support or restrain the cooling assembly where required, then release the sump fasteners and remove the pan.
Clean both mating surfaces until dry and oil-free; keep debris out of the engine.

installation.text: Apply sealant only at the documented K4M bead and junction locations, then position the pan and anti-slosh plate correctly.
Tighten the sump fasteners in the stated sequence, then reinstall removed braces and underbody panels.
Refill with the correct engine oil and inspect carefully for leaks.

checks: No oil leak at the pan joint.
Oil level is correct after settling.
No sealant extrusion into the sump.

name: Oil sump drain plug
summary: Oil drain plug torque and washer replacement policy were not verified in a fetched K4M-specific source; do not infer a value.
safety: Use a stable, level work surface and support the vehicle securely.
Hot oil can cause burns; allow the oil to cool to a safe handling temperature.
tools: Replacement sealing washer if required by the exact plug design

torques.notes: No K4M drain-plug torque was verified in fetched sources.

removal.text: Position a drain pan and remove the plug carefully, avoiding contact with hot oil.
Inspect the plug threads and sealing face; replace a damaged washer or plug.

installation.text: Refit the plug squarely and tighten only to a verified K4M specification; do not substitute a generic value.
Refill the engine, check the oil level and inspect the plug for seepage.

checks: No leakage at the plug after refill.
Oil level is correct on level ground.

name: Camshaft / rocker cover gasket
summary: K4M cover-gasket torque and the specific sealing procedure were not confirmed in fetched sources; the instructions avoid guessed values.
safety: Work on a cool engine and keep dirt out of the exposed cylinder head.
Disconnect the battery before disturbing nearby electrical connectors.

torques.notes: No K4M cover fastener torque was verified.

removal.text: Remove covers and components that obstruct access, labelling electrical plugs and hoses before disconnecting them.
Release the cover evenly and lift it without prying against sealing surfaces.
Remove old gasket material and inspect the cover for cracks, distortion and oil-filled plug wells.

installation.text: Fit the correct new gasket and any required well seals; apply sealant only where the vehicle-specific procedure specifies it.
Seat the cover evenly and tighten in the manufacturer sequence using a verified torque value before reconnecting hoses and wiring.

checks: No oil seepage around the cover or plug wells.
Ignition connectors are secure and the engine idles normally.

name: Intake camshaft dephaser / VVT pulley
summary: The K4M uses a continuously controlled intake camshaft dephaser. Its internal operation is described by the fetched source; removal and bolt torque must follow the exact timing procedure.
safety: Treat this as a timing-critical repair; support and lock the engine using the K4M-specific tools.
Do not loosen the camshaft pulley or dephaser with the engine unrestrained.
Incorrect cam timing can cause severe engine damage.

torques.notes: The fetched source describes K4M operation, not a component-removal torque.

specs.label: Dephasing range
specs.value: Continuously variable from 0 to 43 crankshaft degrees

sources.title: Renault Mégane II workshop manual: Déphaseur d’arbre à cames (K4M)

removal.text: Diagnose the control solenoid, wiring and oil condition before dismantling timing components.
If mechanical access is required, use the complete K4M timing lock and support procedure; do not rely on paint marks alone.
Remove the timing belt and retain the correct relationship between crankshaft and camshaft before removing the dephaser.

installation.text: Install the correct dephaser and any required new fasteners using the exact K4M tightening procedure; no unverified torque is supplied here.
Restore timing-belt tension, rotate the engine by hand and recheck timing alignment before starting.
Clear only relevant diagnostic codes and confirm commanded cam timing and idle quality with suitable diagnostic equipment.

checks: No timing fault codes or unstable idle.
No abnormal mechanical noise.
Cam timing and belt tension are confirmed before first start.

name: Inlet manifold / intake distribution chamber
summary: The K4M intake chamber procedure requires releasing the throttle body, vacuum and fuel connections, wiring and all sealing joints.
safety: Disconnect the battery before disturbing intake wiring.
Depressurize the fuel system and protect the alternator from fuel spills.
Do not damage the brake-booster vacuum outlet on the manifold.

removal.text: Disconnect the battery and remove the engine covers and intake duct.
Disconnect the throttle connector, brake-booster vacuum hose, vapor-recirculation hose and wiring harness; release the fuel feed carefully.
Remove the manifold fasteners in a controlled sequence and lift the intake chamber without forcing the vacuum outlet.

installation.text: Replace all disturbed manifold seals and reinstall the chamber in the proper order.
Tighten manifold fasteners in the illustrated sequence; refit and tighten the motorized throttle body separately.
Reconnect fuel, vacuum, vapor and electrical connections, then reconnect the battery and perform required idle/throttle learning.

checks: No intake or fuel leaks.
Brake-booster vacuum hose is fully seated.
Throttle adaptation completes and idle is stable.

name: Electronic throttle body
summary: K4M throttle-body fastening torque and gasket replacement are documented in the fetched Renault reproduction; a diagnostic adaptation may be required after replacement.
safety: Disconnect the battery before unplugging the throttle actuator.
Do not force the electronic throttle plate by hand.

removal.text: Disconnect the battery, remove the intake duct and unplug the throttle-body connector and vapor hose.
Remove the throttle-body fasteners and lift the unit away without damaging the mating surface.

installation.text: Fit a new gasket, position the throttle body and tighten its fasteners evenly to the sourced torque.
Reconnect hoses and wiring, reconnect the battery, and perform throttle-stop learning with a suitable diagnostic tool if required.

checks: No intake leaks.
Throttle learns its end stops and responds smoothly.
No throttle-related warning or fault remains.

name: Fuel rail and injectors
summary: The K4M fuel-rail procedure warns of fuel spray and requires new injector O-rings and retaining clips when injectors are removed.
safety: Relieve fuel pressure before opening a fuel connection and protect the alternator from fuel spills.
Keep sparks, flames and hot work away from spilled fuel.
Maintain cleanliness; do not allow debris into open injectors or the fuel rail.

removal.text: Disconnect the battery and relieve fuel pressure using the proper method before opening the fuel system.
Remove the intake manifold as required, unplug the injector harness, release the rail fasteners and withdraw the rail carefully.
On a clean work surface, release injector clips and remove injectors without damaging the bores.

installation.text: Fit new injector O-rings and retaining clips; lubricate seals only with a fuel-compatible lubricant if the exact service instruction allows it.
Seat injectors and rail evenly, tighten rail fasteners to the sourced value, and reconnect the fuel and electrical connections.
Prime the system and inspect all joints for leaks before starting.

checks: No fuel leaks at the rail or injector seals.
Engine starts and idles evenly.
No injector circuit faults remain.

name: In-tank fuel filter / pump module
summary: For the fetched K4M application, the petrol filter is integrated into the in-tank pump/gauge module and is not separately removable. Do not treat it as a routine inline-filter service.
safety: Fuel vapour is flammable; work in a ventilated area with ignition sources removed.
Relieve fuel pressure and disconnect the battery before opening the fuel system.
Replace the complete pump/gauge assembly only when its diagnosis indicates failure.

Keep contaminants out of the tank and fuel lines.

installation.text: Install the correct complete module and seal, reconnect fuel and electrical connections, and secure the access cover.
Prime the system and check for fuel leaks and correct operation.

checks: No fuel leaks or fuel odour.
Fuel pressure and delivery meet the vehicle-specific diagnostic specification.

Support the exhaust line before releasing flanges or brackets.
Renew manifold and exhaust-flange gaskets and manifold nuts as specified.
tools: Vehicle lift or rated axle stands

Remove the upstream sensor with the correct tool, heat shields and manifold nuts; lift the manifold clear.

installation.text: Install new manifold and flange gaskets and new manifold nuts.
Tighten the K4M manifold nuts in the specified order, then refit heat shields, sensors, supports and exhaust flange.
Reconnect the battery and inspect heat shields, exhaust clearance and joints for leaks.

checks: No exhaust leak or contact with the underbody.
Heat shields are secure.
Oxygen-sensor wiring is routed away from hot or moving parts.

safety: Work only when the exhaust is cool.
Avoid twisting or trapping the sensor wiring.

Inspect the threads and harness routing before fitting a replacement.

installation.text: Install the correct sensor without contaminating its sensing tip; tighten to the sourced value.
Reconnect the plug and route the lead away from the exhaust.

checks: No exhaust leak at the sensor boss.
Sensor connector is locked and diagnostic readings respond normally.

name: Downstream oxygen (lambda) sensor
summary: The downstream oxygen sensor is removed with a dedicated sensor socket and tightened to the shared sourced torque.
safety: Work only when the exhaust is cool.
Avoid twisting or trapping the sensor wiring.

Reconnect the plug, secure the lead away from heat and clear diagnostic codes only after the repair is verified.

checks: No leak at the sensor boss.
Catalyst-monitor readings and warning status are checked with suitable diagnostics.

name: Rear silencer / exhaust rear section

safety: Support the exhaust securely before releasing hangers or sleeves.
Work only when the exhaust is cool.
Do not reuse a used exhaust sleeve/manchon.

Cut or separate the pipe only at the vehicle-specific joint location; remove the silencer from its supports.
Inspect hangers, heat shields and pipe ends for damage or corrosion.

installation.text: Fit the silencer and a new sleeve, support the exhaust while aligning the complete line, then tighten the hanger supports.
Check all heat shields and confirm that the exhaust has no underbody contact before lowering the vehicle.

checks: No exhaust leaks, rattles or underbody contact.
Silencer hangs without preload or strain.
Heat shields are secure.

name: Right-hand engine mount
summary: Engine-mount torque is shown only in an image on the fetched K4M suspension-mount page and could not be read reliably; no numerical torque is supplied.
safety: Support the engine with an approved support beam before loosening the mount.
Never work beneath an unsupported engine or vehicle.

torques.notes: The K4M/JR5 page displays torque charts as images; readable fastener values were unavailable.

removal.text: Support the engine securely and remove covers or the belt drive needed for access.
Mark mount orientation, then release the body and engine-side fasteners without allowing the engine to shift.

installation.text: Position the replacement mount in its original orientation and start all fasteners by hand.
Align the powertrain without stressing hoses or wiring; tighten only to a verified K4M/JR5 specification before removing the support.

checks: Mount is seated without preload.
No abnormal vibration or contact after start.

name: Gearbox-side mount
summary: The K4M/JR5 suspension-mount page contains a torque chart as an image; a trustworthy numerical value was not available from its text extraction.
safety: Support both the engine and gearbox before mount removal.
Do not allow the transaxle to hang from the driveshafts or wiring.

safety: Use a suitable gearbox support; the transmission must not be allowed to fall.
The clutch disc and cover must be kept free of oil and grease.
This is a heavy drivetrain job; use an adequately rated lift and transmission jack.

Lock the flywheel with the specified tool, remove the pressure-plate fasteners progressively and separate the disc and cover.
Inspect the flywheel and input-shaft splines; keep friction surfaces clean and dry.

installation.text: Install the disc in the correct orientation and centre it with the alignment tool.
Fit the pressure plate and tighten its fasteners progressively in a star pattern to the K4M torque.
Remove the flywheel lock, install the release bearing/slave cylinder as applicable, and reinstall the gearbox without forcing the input shaft.

checks: Clutch engages and releases smoothly.

Gearbox is fully seated and all removed connections are restored.

Do not press the clutch pedal with the hydraulic circuit disconnected.

installation.text: Install a new slave-cylinder/release-bearing assembly and new hydraulic seals; connect the line without cross-threading.

Support the front of the vehicle securely when removing wheel-arch parts.

removal.text: Disconnect the battery, remove front access parts and release the accessory belt.
Disconnect alternator electrical connectors, then remove the mounting fasteners and withdraw the unit without stressing air-conditioning lines.

installation.text: Compress the alternator mounting bushings as needed for fitment and reinstall the unit without forcing the bracket.
Reconnect wiring, refit and tension the accessory belt, reinstall front-end parts and reconnect the battery.

checks: Charging voltage and warning lamp are normal.
No belt noise, misalignment or cable heating.
